ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure, the horizontal axis is labeled Kinetic energy, and the vertical axis is labeled Number of Ne atoms. The curve rises rapidly from the low kinetic energy end, reaches a peak near between B and C, at a position slightly to the left of C, and then slowly decreases to the right, forming a very long high-energy tail. The letter A is at the leftmost low-energy place, B is near the left side of the peak, C is slightly to the right of the peak, and D is farther to the right and has already entered the obvious tail region. Then reason: This distribution is asymmetric, with a long tail on the right side, so the most probable kinetic energy is near the peak, while the average kinetic energy will be pulled higher by the high-energy tail on the right side, and its position should be slightly to the right of the peak. The letter C in the figure is exactly slightly to the right of the peak; D is too far to the right, indicating a too-deep tail region. Therefore the average kinetic energy is labeled C.

Identify the most probable kinetic energy near the peak, then place the average slightly to the right of that peak because the tail raises the mean. Among the letters, C is the label just to the right of the peak and D is too far into the tail, so the average kinetic energy is C.
